title: Going Deep - Models for Continuous Time Within Play Valuation of Game Outcomes in American Football with Tracking Data
file_name: Going Deep - Models for Continuous Time Within Play Valuation of Game Outcomes in American Football with Tracking Data.md
universal_lens: A continuous-time valuation framework for American football leveraging tracking data to assess dynamic game outcomes through modular sub-models and LSTM-based ball-carrier estimation. Voronoi tessellations encode spatial dominance; neural networks map positional features to continuous-valued outcome expectations.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference over tracking-derived play states using conformal predictive distributions for expected points and win probability updates within-play. Bayesian inference on Voronoi-derived spatial features enables probabilistic valuation of ball-carrier movement trajectories using conformal prediction.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning engine mapping player trajectories and game state transitions via continuous-time Markov processes informed by LSTM-based positional forecasting. Situational reasoning integrates Voronoi-based spatial metrics with recurrent state transitions to predict play evolution and expected points.

primitives.name: Ball Carrier Voronoi Region Area
primitives.verbatim_quote: > We extract three simple features from the Voronoi tessellation: the area of the Voronoi region associated with the ball carrier, and the x-coordinates of the closest and farthest points from the target endzone on the boundary of the ball-carrier's Voronoi region.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{\\text{bc}}': 'Area of the Voronoi region assigned to the ball carrier, measured in square yards'}
primitives.assumptions: Players are modeled as points in a 2D Euclidean space; Voronoi regions are convex polygons defined by perpendicular bisectors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ball carrier is isolated or surrounded by an equal number of teammates and defenders, resulting in degenerate Voronoi cells.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 1 introduces a foundational framework for continuous-time within-play valuation in American football using Next Gen Stats tracking data. It establishes that prior methods relied on discrete-time estimates due to limitations in available datasets. The core innovation lies in modeling the evolution of play outcomes through time, rather than treating them as static events. The framework integrates modular components including a ball-carrier model, which uses LSTM networks to predict yardage gains based on real-time tracking inputs. These predictions are then fed into a between-play model to compute expected points or win probabilities. The approach enables dynamic assessment of strategic decisions and player performance throughout the duration of a play. This methodology aligns with broader trends in sports analytics toward granular, real-time decision support systems. The use of LSTM networks reflects a shift towards machine learning paradigms capable of handling sequential data with long-range dependencies. The framework's adaptability allows integration of various existing models for expected points and win probability, enhancing its utility across different analytical contexts. The emphasis on tracking data over traditional play-by-play metrics underscores the increasing sophistication of data-driven sports science. The paper's contribution lies in bridging the gap between high-frequency tracking data and meaningful game-theoretic evaluations.

reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 introduces a methodological framework for modeling ball-carrier behavior in American football using tracking data. It begins by leveraging Voronoi tessellations to capture spatial dominance dynamics around the ball carrier. These geometric constructs provide a natural way to quantify the amount of space controlled by the ball carrier relative to surrounding players. The extracted features—area of the Voronoi region and boundary extremes—are then fed into machine learning models. The paper evaluates several architectures including LASSO, XGBoost, feedforward neural networks, and LSTM variants. The LSTM emerges as the most effective model based on cross-validation metrics, suggesting that temporal dependencies in player movement are crucial for accurate prediction. This chapter establishes a foundation for integrating geometric spatial features with deep learning techniques to assess real-time game states and forecast outcomes. The implications extend beyond immediate tactical insights to broader applications in strategic planning and performance analytics.
